Do NOT edit other files. Note: another agent edits dispatch_auth.rs lines ~214-230, ~370-395, ~460-470, ~578-586 — stay strictly inside the ~95-120 region to avoid overlap.

# Change (five items, all verified open at head b4c00985)
1. **fetch_workflows ignores git_ref in local workspaces (P1)** — `crate::github::fetch_workflows_at` (github.rs ~line 567) and its sibling `fetch_workflows` (~line 558) return the CHECKED-OUT `.github/workflows` directory when `shared.state.local_workspace` is set, ignoring `git_ref`. A dispatch for a branch different from the checked-out tree then reads the wrong workflow definitions. Fix: in the local-workspace branch, resolve the requested `git_ref` via git: `git -C <workspace> rev-parse --verify <git_ref>^{commit}`; if it resolves, list files with `git -C <workspace> ls-tree -r --name-only <git_ref> -- .github/workflows` and read each with `git -C <workspace> show <git_ref>:<path>` (file names end `.yml`/`.yaml`, same filter as today; entries are `path/to/name.yml` — take the basename as the workflow key exactly as the current code does with `file_name`). If the ref does NOT resolve locally (e.g. the workspace never fetched that branch), fall back to the current checked-out-tree behavior with a `warn!` log (preserve existing behavior for that case — do not fail the dispatch). Keep the remote path (`fetch_remote_workflows`) and the no-credential fallback unchanged. Use `tokio::process::Command` like `resolve_default_branch` does (dispatch.rs ~line 549) — `git` commands run async; parse stdout as UTF-8 defensively (`String::from_utf8_lossy` or filter `Ok`).
2. **origin/ prefix not stripped (P1)** — `resolve_default_branch` in dispatch.rs (~line 554-563): `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` returns `origin/<branch>` (e.g. `origin/main`) when `origin/HEAD` exists, so the caller builds `refs/heads/origin/main` and dispatches fail or target the wrong ref. Fix: after trimming, strip a leading `origin/` prefix before returning (`branch.strip_prefix("origin/").unwrap_or(branch)`).
3. **Hardcoded `main` fallback (P2)** — same function: when `origin/HEAD` is absent it returns `"main"`. Fix: before falling back to `"main"`, try `git -C <workspace> symbolic-ref --short HEAD` (the currently checked-out branch) and return that if non-empty and valid; keep `"main"` only as the final fallback (e.g. detached HEAD).
4. **repository_dispatch gated on actions:write (P2, verified against github.com docs)** — `authorize_dispatch` in dispatch.rs (~line 314-330) requires `has_actions_write()` for BOTH dispatch POSTs. github.com gates `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dispatches` on `contents: write` and workflow dispatch on `actions: write`. Fix: split into two functions: `authorize_workflow_dispatch` (keep current behavior: `covers_repository` + `has_actions_write`) used by `workflow_dispatch` (~line 38), and `authorize_repository_dispatch` (same `covers_repository` check + new `identity.has_contents_write()`) used by `repository_dispatch` (~line 130). Update the doc comments ("Shared authorization for the dispatch POSTs" becomes per-endpoint docs naming the required permission). Keep `authorize_read` unchanged.
5. **has_contents_write on DispatchIdentity (P2)** — in dispatch_auth.rs next to `has_actions_write` (~line 102), add `pub(crate) fn has_contents_write(&self) -> bool` mirroring it exactly: installation tokens check `token.permissions.get("contents")` is `write`|`admin`; every other kind returns `true`. Follow the existing doc-comment style. Do not touch anything else in the file.

# Acceptance
- All changes compile-read coherently (no undefined symbols; `warn!`/`info!` imports present — dispatch.rs already imports `warn` and `info`).
- The local-workspace ref resolution must not regress the no-`git_ref` case: if `git_ref` is empty, skip resolution and use the checked-out tree (guard against empty ref).
- Do NOT run cargo. Report per item: exact changes and functions touched.

## Changes (worktree `/Users/bnjoroge/preloop-gh-app-api-compat`, head b4c00985)

**1. `fetch_workflows` ignores git_ref in local workspaces (P1)** — `crates/preloop-runner-server/src/github.rs`, `fetch_workflows_at` (local-workspace branch only)
- Guarded by `!git_ref.is_empty()` (empty ref skips resolution, uses checked-out tree as before).
- Resolves the ref: `git -C <workspace> rev-parse --verify <ref>^{commit}` via `tokio::process::Command`.
- On success: `git ls-tree -r --name-only <ref> -- .github/workflows`, then per `.yml`/`.yaml` entry (basename check, same filter as today) reads `git show <ref>:<path>`, keyed by basename via `path.rsplit('/').next()`; returns the map (silently skips failed `show`, matching the remote path's skip-on-failure behavior).
- On unresolved ref: `warn!` log (workspace field) + falls through to the existing checked-out-tree directory walk — behavior preserved, dispatch not failed.
- Remote path (`fetch_remote_workflows`) and the no-credential `PathBuf::from(".")` fallback untouched. `warn!` was already imported in github.rs.

**2. `origin/` prefix not stripped (P1)** — `dispatch.rs`, `resolve_default_branch`: after trimming `symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` output, strips a leading `origin/` (`trimmed.strip_prefix("origin/").unwrap_or(trimmed)`) so `origin/main` → `main` and callers build `refs/heads/main`.

**3. Hardcoded `main` fallback (P2)** — same function: when `origin/HEAD` is absent/unusable, tries `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` (checked-out branch) and returns it if non-empty and space-free; `"main"` is now only the final fallback (detached HEAD). Remote API path unchanged.

**4. repository_dispatch gated on actions:write (P2)** — `dispatch.rs`
- `authorize_dispatch` split into `authorize_workflow_dispatch` (`covers_repository` + `has_actions_write`) used by `workflow_dispatch` (line 44) and `authorize_repository_dispatch` (`covers_repository` + new `has_contents_write`) used by `repository_dispatch` (line 136). Both keep the same 403 message shape, naming the respective permission.
- Doc comments rewritten per-endpoint; module-header 403 error-semantics doc updated to "no `actions: write` or `contents: write`". `authorize_read` unchanged. No stale `authorize_dispatch` references remain (grep-verified).

**5. `has_contents_write` on DispatchIdentity (P2)** — `dispatch_auth.rs`, inserted directly after `has_actions_write` (lines ~117-133, well clear of the sibling agent's regions at ~214-230/370-395/460-470/578-586): mirrors it exactly — installation tokens check `token.permissions.get("contents")` for `write`|`admin`, all other kinds return `true`; same doc-comment style.

## Verification
- Grep: no remaining `authorize_dispatch`; `has_contents_write` defined (dispatch_auth.rs) and used (dispatch.rs); `warn!`/`info!` still used in dispatch.rs (lines 205/217) so imports stay live.
